children: The S&P Global Taiwan Manufacturing PMI fell to 54.9 in October 2026 from a more than five-year high of 56.7 in the previous month.
Nevertheless, it marked the eleventh consecutive month of expansion, supported by continued growth in new orders amid improving demand conditions across domestic and export markets.
Output also increased for another month, although at a slower pace, while employment rose for the fourth consecutive month as manufacturers sought to keep pace with rising workloads.
Meanwhile, supplier delivery times lengthened markedly in October as strong AI-related demand strained capacity and shipping delays persisted amid the Middle East conflict.
On the price front, input costs climbed sharply again, albeit at a slightly slower pace than in September, reflecting higher prices for metals, plastics and electronics.
Lastly, business confidence edged lower but stayed above the series average.

title: Taiwan Manufacturing Maintains Momentum
